newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WHO warns travellers about meningitis in Romania.
newsitem.headline: WHO warns travellers about meningitis in Romania.

text.p: The World Health Organisation (WHO), reporting figures by the Romanian Health Ministry, said on Tuesday that an outbreak of viral meningitis around Bucharest had struck 450 people since late July, causing 39 deaths.
In a statement, the United Nations agency said it opposed quarantine measures or travel restrictions to and from Romania as they had "no effect" in containing the spread of the mosquito-borne virus.

But WHO recommended tourists or business travellers to wear protective clothing and insect repellant to avoid catching the virus, whose spread is expected to decline with the start of winter. Twenty-six patients remain hospitalised in Bucharest.

Laboratory tests conducted by WHO at the Pasteur Institute in Paris confirmed that the patients, mainly elderly living in within 80 km (50 miles) of Bucharest, are suffering from the West Nile virus, according to the statement issued in Geneva.
There is no specific drug treatment for the virus, which causes fever and can degenerate into a fatal inflammation of the brain, known as meningoencephalitis.
"The outbreak in Romania is expected to decline with the onset of colder weather, which will rapidly reduce the population of Culex mosquitos," WHO said.
